answer: To prevent an autonomous juniper biomass exchange from becoming a haven for Sybil actors, the network uses collateralized peer-vouching with quadratic slashing. Joining agents must secure slashable bonds from established nodes, forcing attackers to lock scarce financial capital that enters a liquidation spiral upon detected fraud. This imposes a strictly non-zero capital cost per identity. However, steep collateral thresholds inevitably marginalize honest, underfunded participants.
